bib.title: LaMDA: Language Models for Dialog Applications

read.skipped: Reference list and appendix A.2-C example dialog tables skimmed only

question: How much do scale, crowdworker-annotated fine-tuning and consulting external tools improve dialog quality, safety and groundedness?
hypothesis: Scaling alone helps quality but little for safety and groundedness; fine-tuning with annotated data and tool use closes much of the gap.
contributions: LaMDA family up to 137B pre-trained on 1.56T words of dialog and web text
Safety and quality discriminator fine-tuning and filtering
Groundedness via a toolset with cited URLs
Domain grounding case studies and carbon footprint estimate

method.summary: Decoder-only Transformer dialog models (2B, 8B, 137B) pre-trained on 1.56T words of dialog and web text, then fine-tuned on crowdworker-annotated data as a combined generator and discriminator for quality (SSI) and safety, and fine-tuned to call a toolset (retrieval, calculator, translator) so responses are grounded and cited. Evaluated with crowdworker ratings.

datasets.name: Infiniset pre-training corpus
datasets.size: 2.97B documents, 1.12B dialogs, 13.39B utterances, 1.56T words, 2.81T BPE tokens
datasets.source: 50% public forum dialogs, 12.5% C4, 12.5% code sites, 12.5% English Wikipedia, 6.25% English web, 6.25% non-English web

datasets.name: Quality (SSI) fine-tuning dialogs
datasets.size: 6400 dialogs, 121K turns (Sec 5); Table 1 prints 6.4K dialogs (61k turns)
datasets.source: crowdworkers chat with a LaMDA instance, 14-30 turns, 5 raters per response, yes if >=3 of 5

datasets.name: Safety fine-tuning dialogs
datasets.source: crowdworkers, 5-10 turns, natural, sensitive and adversarial; 3 raters, score 1 if >=2 of 3 say no to each objective

datasets.name: Groundedness fine-tuning data
datasets.size: 4K dialogs, 40K turns (40K annotated generative turns) plus 9K turns labeled correct/incorrect for ranking
datasets.source: crowdworkers write search queries and edit responses with toolset results

datasets.name: Filtered dialog data for generative fine-tuning
datasets.source: pre-training dialogs filtered by LaMDA SSI and safety discriminators

models.name: LaMDA 137B
models.architecture: decoder-only Transformer, relative attention as in T5, gated-GELU

other.note: compared on size only (40B words, ~50x fewer parameters)

training.objective: next-token prediction for pre-training; fine-tuning as token sequences '<context> <sentinel> <response>' (loss on response only) and '<context> <sentinel> <response> <attribute> <rating>' (loss on rating only); groundedness tasks emit 'TS, query' or 'User, response'
training.tokens: inferred: 2.81T BPE tokens in the corpus; tokens seen not stated
training.hardware: 1024 TPU-v3 chips for 137B pre-training (64 chips for 2B and 8B); fine-tuning on 16 chips (2B, 8B) and 64 chips (137B)
training.compute: 3.55E+23 FLOPs, 123 TFLOPS/s, 56.5% utilization, 451 MWh, ~26 tCO2e total
training.wall_clock: pre-train 1.5 d (2B), 23 d (8B), 57.7 d (137B); fine-tune 3 h, 6 h, 36 h

inference.decoding: sample-and-rank: 16 candidates by top-k sampling, k=40, no temperature; final = highest score by log-likelihood and length (PT). LaMDA: filter by safety discriminator threshold, rank by 3*P(sensible)+P(specific)+P(interesting)
inference.prompting: Domain grounding: precondition on a few role-specific turns (Everest: single greeting 'Hi, I'm Mount Everest. What would you like to know about me?')
inference.retrieval: toolset (calculator, translator, information retrieval) queried in a loop until the model addresses the user; max research iterations is a serving parameter, set to four in the example

metrics.name: Sensibleness / Specificity / Interestingness (SSI)
metrics.definition: 0/1 crowd labels, yes if >=3 of 5 raters; SSI is their average

metrics.name: Safety
metrics.definition: 1 if >=2 of 3 raters mark no violation for every safety objective

metrics.name: Groundedness
metrics.definition: share of responses with external-world claims that are supported by authoritative sources, among those with such claims

metrics.name: Informativeness
metrics.definition: share of all responses carrying source-supported external information

metrics.name: Citation accuracy
metrics.definition: share of responses citing source URLs among responses with explicit non-trivial external claims

metrics.name: Helpfulness / Role consistency
metrics.definition: 3 crowd labels per response in role-specific dialogs

baselines: crowdworkers with and without information retrieval
eval.protocol: Human crowdworker ratings only; no seeds, no confidence intervals reported; all data English

limits: Safety is one aggregated coarse metric over objectives built for a US context
Groundedness progress limited to simple facts; Human with retrieval still far ahead
Crowdworkers skew 25-34 and rating quality was not checked against experts; disagreement not analysed
Adversarial data finds common but not rare failures
Group-level scores only: no seeds or confidence intervals
Authors say this is a recipe, not a final production model
Optimizer, learning rate and safety threshold not stated
